action.name: HTML Framer
action.description: LOOM core bridge for turning uploaded static HTML ZIP packages into isolated, portable project modules with compatibility Action Reader telemetry.

admin_settings.title: HTML Framer
admin_settings.description: Drop static HTML ZIP packages into LOOM. Smart auto-fit preserves foreign app layout. Frames default to 80% of the usable page width so the surrounding LOOM page remains easy to scroll; any individual frame can optionally start interaction-locked and be unlocked from a centered control.

fields.label: Enable HTML Framer modules
fields.help: When off, stored HTML frames remain preserved in the Instance Vault but are not added to the project runtime.

fields.label: Desktop height behavior
fields.help: Auto-fit is the default. LOOM detects ordinary document pages versus viewport-style apps/games. Documents grow with content; viewport apps keep their intentional 100%-height/internal-layout contract without shell oscillation.

fields.label: Desktop fixed height
fields.help: Used only when Desktop height behavior is Fixed.

fields.label: Desktop page width
fields.help: Percentage of the usable project page width. Default is 80%, leaving page gutters available for normal LOOM scrolling.

fields.label: Mobile height behavior
fields.help: Independent mobile behavior at 760px and below. Smart auto-fit preserves responsive document flow and viewport-style mobile apps without creating an iframe scrollbar.

fields.label: Mobile fixed height
fields.help: Used only when Mobile height behavior is Fixed.

fields.label: Mobile page width
fields.help: Independent phone/narrow-screen width. Default is 80%; Admin can raise it to 100% when a full-bleed mobile app is intentional.

fields.label: Allow full-screen frame control by default
fields.help: New HTML frames receive a Full screen control that temporarily takes over the browser viewport and hides LOOM chrome. Admin can disable the control per frame.

fields.label: Framed Action Reader
fields.help: Automatically instruments framed HTML controls and turns observable clicks, navigation, form submits, and field changes into LOOM user actions. Does not capture typed field values.
